findings.title: Buffer overflow or out-of-bounds read
findings.trigger: If int_type->name points to a string longer than the buffer allocated for it, a buffer overflow can occur.
findings.assumptions: The parser does not properly validate the length of the name string before allocating memory or copying it into int_type->name.

findings.title: OS command injection
findings.trigger: If the source_code string is crafted in a way that it contains malicious commands, and the parser executes these commands, it could lead to OS command injection.
findings.assumptions: The create_parser function or any function it calls might execute commands based on the input string.

findings.title: Integer overflow or wraparound
findings.trigger: If the values of int_type->min_value or int_type->max_value are not properly validated, they could cause integer overflow or wraparound when printed.
findings.assumptions: The values of min_value and max_value are derived from the parsed source_code without proper bounds checking.

findings.title: Improper resource management
findings.trigger: If int_type->name or int_type were not properly allocated or if they were freed multiple times, it could lead to undefined behavior.
findings.assumptions: The memory allocation and deallocation logic in the parser is correct and follows a consistent pattern.
